additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional disorder is characterized by one or more persistent, non-bizarre or less obviously bizarre delusions lasting at least one month, in the absence of prominent hallucinations, disorganized thought, or marked mood episodes that would suggest schizophrenia or a major mood disorder with psychotic features. Outside of the delusional beliefs, functioning can be relatively preserved, and behavior may appear largely appropriate, which often delays recognition and treatment. The content of the delusions tends to be systematized (e.g., persecutory, jealous, somatic, grandiose, or erotomanic themes) and is held with strong conviction despite clear contradictory evidence. The course is often chronic, with limited insight and variable impact on social and occupational functioning, and it can be distinguished from obsessive thoughts by the lack of perceived egodystonicity and resistance.

patient.stressor: Roy’s difficulties began after he took on a series of high-stakes technical translation contracts for a new European client, where strict non-disclosure agreements and complex encryption protocols heightened his preexisting anxiety about accuracy and confidentiality. Around eleven months ago, after a dispute over minor terminology choices and a tense video call in which a project manager questioned his work, he started to fixate on the idea that his translations were being secretly scrutinized and used for purposes beyond what was stated in the contracts. Over the following months, he became increasingly preoccupied with perceived hidden agendas in email instructions and quality audits, which began to color how he interacted with colleagues and clients, even as he continued to meet deadlines and outwardly function in his role. His wife eventually urged him to seek psychiatric care when his insistence on these beliefs started to interfere with family travel plans and he refused a promising promotion because he was convinced upper management was monitoring him for reasons they would not disclose.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep holding on to this belief that my clients and managers are secretly monitoring and using my translations in ways they deny, and nothing anyone says can convince me otherwise.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Ever since that argument about my word choices on the video call, I’ve been absolutely convinced that my translations are being fed into some hidden system and dissected line by line by people way above my managers, and no matter how many times my wife or colleagues tell me it’s just routine QA, I can see in the phrasing of the emails and the odd timing of their ‘random’ checks that they’re tracking me for something they’re not admitting.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: Day to day I still hit my deadlines, handle complex technical projects, and my clients keep sending work my way, but the only real problems that have come up—like turning down that promotion or arguing with my wife about work trips—are directly because of my conviction that the company is secretly monitoring how my translations are being used.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Aside from refusing that promotion and avoiding certain projects and business trips because I’m sure they’re part of this hidden monitoring, I’m still working full-time, paying bills, and taking care of things at home pretty much as before.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about eleven months now, ever since that tense video call where they challenged my wording and I started to feel convinced my translations were being secretly scrutinized.
